svg.text: ALINA — architecture overview (current state, LLM wiki excluded)
AI Legal Intelligence Assistant for DG DIGIT Unit R.3 · one bespoke web application + two Commission platform services (AI@EC, GPT@EC) · 1 October 2026
Users — Commission staff only (no external users)
DIGIT.R3 procurement officers, contract managers and legal officers (project members) · project administrators (corpus curation per procedure) · application
administrators (user accounts). Web browser over HTTPS, desktop, English.
HTTPS: sign in (email + password), ask questions, manage projects, documents and users

Container host — Railway (pilot). One Docker image: Next.js 16 standalone server + LibreOffice; migrations and admin bootstrap run at container start. Previously AWS ECS Fargate (Phase 1, decommissioned).
ALINA application (Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript) — the only bespoke component

• Documents — upload, document type and authority

password from the users table, 8 h JWT session cookie, 5 failed

indexing or configuration (no persistent feedback loop

off (answer taken from the result event)
• State: documents (accumulated across tool calls, global [n] numbering) · filters
(entitlement, injected server-side, hidden from the model, ANDed into every retrieval)
• System prompt: resolve a named document first, answer from the highest-authority source,
verbatim quotes with [n], refuse when the corpus is silent, English, no legal advice
• BM25 top 30 (fuzziness 0) ‖ e5-base-v2 dense top 30 → reciprocal rank fusion
• Sentence-window expansion ±1 chunk (by file_id and split_id)
• Second Qwen3 reranking pass, top 30, calibrated scores (shown in the UI)
• MetaFieldGroupingRanker: group by authority_rank, subgroup by file_id, sort by split_id
• result_formatter: global [n] continuing from state, dedup against state, ≤ 30 documents
and ≤ 12 000 characters per call; new documents appended to state
